subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The principle of postural drainage is to:

options.B: Position the patient so the affected bronchopulmonary segment is uppermost, allowing gravity to assist secretion drainage
options.C: Place the affected segment lowest to increase perfusion
options.D: Make the patient lie supine for all segments

questions.explanation: The segmental bronchus is positioned vertically with the segment above it so secretions drain toward the larger airways, helped by percussion, vibration and coughing.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To drain the apical segments of both upper lobes the patient is positioned:

options.B: Sitting upright, leaning slightly back or forward
options.C: Prone with the foot of the bed raised

questions.explanation: Apical bronchi are directed upward; sitting is the drainage position. Bases require head-down tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The lateral basal segment of the right lower lobe is drained with the patient lying:

options.A: On the right side with the foot end elevated
options.D: On the left side with the foot end elevated about 20 degrees

questions.explanation: The side to be drained is uppermost; the foot of the bed is raised (head-down) to align the lower lobe bronchus with gravity.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Head-down postural drainage should be avoided in patients with:

options.A: Raised intracranial pressure, uncontrolled hypertension or acute heart failure

questions.explanation: Head-down tilt increases venous return and intracranial pressure and may precipitate pulmonary oedema or reflux/aspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Percussion (clapping) over the chest wall is performed with:

options.A: Cupped hands in a rhythmic manner over the segment being drained
options.D: A closed fist directly on the spine

questions.explanation: A cupped hand traps air and produces a gentle wave; avoid bony prominences, breasts and the kidney area.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Vibrations are applied to the chest wall:
questions.explanation: Compressive vibration synchronised with expiration helps move secretions; the force is gentle and the hands stay in contact.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The active cycle of breathing technique (ACBT) consists of:

options.D: Breathing control, thoracic expansion exercises and the forced expiration technique

questions.explanation: ACBT cycles include breathing control (relaxed tidal breathing), deep breathing exercises and huffing (FET), repeated until the chest is clear.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A ‘huff’ in the forced expiration technique helps clear secretions from:

options.D: Mid- and peripheral airways when done from mid- to low lung volume

questions.explanation: A huff from mid lung volume mobilises secretions in smaller airways; a huff from high volume clears larger central airways.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An incentive spirometer encourages the patient to:

options.B: Take a slow, maximal sustained inspiration
options.D: Hold the breath after a short sniff

questions.explanation: Sustained maximal inspirations (SMI) improve lung volumes and prevent postoperative atelectasis.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pursed-lip breathing benefits patients with COPD by:

options.D: Prolonging expiration and generating back pressure to keep the small airways open

questions.explanation: It reduces air trapping, lowers respiratory rate and improves exercise tolerance.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: During diaphragmatic breathing the abdomen should:

options.B: Rise on inspiration and fall on expiration

questions.explanation: Diaphragm descends on inspiration, pushing abdominal contents outward.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A patient with abdominal incision should support the wound during coughing by:

options.C: Holding a pillow or hands firmly over the wound (splinting)

questions.explanation: Splinting reduces pain and increases cough effectiveness; adequate analgesia is also important.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The correct sequence of a normal cough is:

options.B: Deep inspiration, glottis closure with raised intrathoracic pressure, then forced expiration with glottis opening

questions.explanation: Inspiration, compression (glottic closure + contraction of expiratory muscles), expulsion.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To stimulate cough by tracheal stimulation the therapist places a finger:

options.A: Over the thyroid cartilage with hard pressure
options.B: Just above the suprasternal notch, pressing gently on the trachea

questions.explanation: A short gentle pressure at the suprasternal notch can elicit cough in patients who cannot cough voluntarily.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Normal chest expansion measured at the level of the nipples is approximately:
questions.explanation: Normal chest expansion ≥5 cm; reduced in ankylosing spondylitis (<2.5 cm).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The hallmark of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on spirometry is:

options.A: A reduced FEV1/FVC ratio (below 70%) that is not fully reversible

questions.explanation: COPD: persistent airflow limitation; FEV1/FVC <0.70 post-bronchodilator.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In COPD (emphysema), which lung volume is typically increased?
questions.explanation: Air trapping increases residual volume and functional residual capacity; vital capacity and FEV1 decrease.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In restrictive lung disease the typical pulmonary function pattern is:

options.B: Reduced FVC with a normal or increased FEV1/FVC ratio

questions.explanation: Restriction reduces all lung volumes proportionally, so the ratio stays normal or high (e.g. pulmonary fibrosis).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Permanent dilatation of the medium-sized bronchi with recurrent infection and copious purulent sputum is:
questions.explanation: Bronchiectasis causes chronic productive cough; treatment includes postural drainage and ACBT; HRCT is diagnostic.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation of the:
questions.explanation: Thick sticky secretions obstruct airways, pancreas and gut; sweat chloride >60 mmol/L is diagnostic.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Asthma is characterised by:

options.C: Reversible airflow obstruction with wheeze, cough and breathlessness

questions.explanation: Bronchial hyper-reactivity and inflammation; PEFR shows diurnal variation >20%.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Exercise-induced bronchospasm is best prevented by:

options.C: Warm-up, a pre-exercise inhaled bronchodilator and breathing through the nose in warm humid air

questions.explanation: Cold, dry air is a trigger; a gradual warm-up and prophylactic β2-agonists help.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A tension pneumothorax presents with:

options.C: Tracheal deviation toward the affected side
options.D: Tracheal deviation away from the affected side, hypotension and absent breath sounds

questions.explanation: A one-way valve increases intrapleural pressure and compresses the mediastinum; requires immediate needle decompression.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Over a large pleural effusion, the percussion note is:
questions.explanation: Dullness with reduced/absent breath sounds and reduced vocal resonance; hyper-resonance occurs in pneumothorax.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Post-operative atelectasis is MOST effectively prevented by:

options.B: Early mobilisation, deep breathing exercises and incentive spirometry

questions.explanation: Reduced lung volumes after anaesthesia and pain contribute; early ambulation and deep breathing restore functional residual capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Consolidation of the lung is associated with:

options.B: Stony dullness with decreased vocal resonance
options.C: Bronchial breathing, dull percussion note and increased vocal resonance

questions.explanation: Solid lung conducts sound better: bronchial breath sounds, whispering pectoriloquy, dull note.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A therapist treating a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis should use:

options.B: A properly fitted N95/FFP2 respirator (airborne precautions)

questions.explanation: TB spreads by airborne droplet nuclei; airborne isolation with N95 masks is required.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which type of isolation requires only the use of a mask?
questions.explanation: Droplet precautions use a mask; contact precautions use gloves and gowns; strict isolation uses all barrier methods.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In acute respiratory distress syndrome, a key supportive position that improves oxygenation is:
questions.explanation: Prone positioning recruits dorsal lung regions and improves V/Q matching; used for at least 12–16 hours/day in severe ARDS.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The best definitive management of a severe flail chest with respiratory failure is:

options.A: Positive pressure ventilation (internal pneumatic stabilisation) with analgesia

questions.explanation: Paradoxical movement is managed by analgesia, oxygen and ventilation if needed; binders restrict breathing.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A normal arterial oxygen saturation is approximately:
questions.explanation: Below 90% indicates hypoxaemia; COPD targets are usually 88–92%.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a patient with COPD and chronic CO2 retention, oxygen therapy is titrated to a saturation of about:
questions.explanation: High FiO2 can suppress hypoxic drive and worsen hypercapnia; controlled low-flow oxygen (Venturi mask) is used.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A Venturi mask delivers:

options.C: A fixed, accurate concentration of oxygen irrespective of the patient's breathing pattern

questions.explanation: A high-flow device using entrainment of air through colour-coded valves.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Nasal cannula oxygen at 2–4 L/min delivers approximately:
questions.explanation: Each litre adds about 4% over the 21% in room air; flows above 4 L/min dry the nasal mucosa.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Hyperventilation produces which acid–base disorder?
questions.explanation: Blowing off CO2 reduces carbonic acid and raises pH; symptoms include perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An ABG shows pH 7.30, PaCO2 60 mmHg and normal bicarbonate. This is:
questions.explanation: Low pH with high PaCO2 and normal HCO3⁻ indicates uncompensated respiratory acidosis (e.g. acute ventilatory failure).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal arterial PaO2 in a healthy adult breathing room air is approximately:
questions.explanation: PaO2 <60 mmHg (8 kPa) defines type 1 respiratory failure; normal PaCO2 is 35–45 mmHg.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) in mechanical ventilation:

options.A: Keeps alveoli open at the end of expiration, improving oxygenation

questions.explanation: PEEP prevents alveolar collapse but may reduce cardiac output and cause barotrauma at high levels.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A speaking valve on a tracheostomy tube may be used only if the cuff is:
questions.explanation: A one-way valve requires an open upper airway for exhalation around the tube, so cuff must be deflated.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Tracheal suction through an endotracheal tube should be limited in duration to about:
questions.explanation: Prolonged suctioning causes hypoxia, vagal bradycardia and trauma; pre-oxygenate and use sterile technique.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Cardiac rehabilitation Phase I refers to:

options.B: The inpatient phase after the cardiac event

questions.explanation: Phase I inpatient (early mobilisation); Phase II early outpatient supervised programme; Phase III maintenance.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The maximum predicted heart rate in a healthy adult is commonly estimated as:
questions.explanation: A 40-year-old: 180 bpm. Moderate intensity is ~64–76% of HRmax.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The original Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion scale runs from:
questions.explanation: The 6–20 scale approximates heart rate/10; the modified CR10 scale runs 0–10. A rating of 12–14 is typical for moderate exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Exercise should be terminated if a cardiac patient develops:

options.C: A heart rate rise of 20 bpm
options.D: Chest pain, marked dyspnoea, dizziness or a drop in systolic BP with exercise

questions.explanation: Warning signs: angina, severe breathlessness, pallor, dizziness, arrhythmias, ST depression >2 mm, hypotensive response.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In uncomplicated acute myocardial infarction, early mobilisation (sitting out of bed) is usually begun within:
questions.explanation: Prolonged bed rest causes deconditioning, DVT and orthostatic intolerance; progress with monitoring.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: After median sternotomy for CABG, patients should AVOID:

options.C: Pushing or pulling with the arms, lifting heavy objects and unsupported coughing

questions.explanation: Sternal precautions for about 6–12 weeks prevent sternal instability: hugging a pillow when coughing, no lifting >2–5 kg, avoid pushing up with the arms.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The drug used sublingually for the relief of an acute angina attack is:
questions.explanation: GTN dilates veins and coronary arteries; patients should carry it during exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In NYHA class III heart failure the patient:

options.B: Has marked limitation: comfortable at rest but less-than-ordinary activity causes symptoms
options.C: Has no symptoms with ordinary activity

questions.explanation: Class I no limitation; II slight limitation; III marked limitation; IV symptoms at rest.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The mitral valve lies between the:
questions.explanation: Mitral (bicuspid) valve prevents backflow into the left atrium; tricuspid is on the right.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The first heart sound (S1) is produced by closure of the:
questions.explanation: S1 ‘lub’ marks the start of ventricular systole; S2 ‘dub’ is semilunar valve closure.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The primary purpose of an arterial line is to:

options.C: Provide continuous blood pressure monitoring and arterial blood sampling

questions.explanation: Intra-arterial catheters, usually radial, give beat-to-beat BP and ABG access.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In patients with hypertension, which type of exercise should be limited?
questions.explanation: Isometric effort and breath-holding cause marked rises in blood pressure; dynamic aerobic exercise lowers resting BP.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which exercise best helps prevent deep vein thrombosis after surgery?

options.D: Ankle pumps (active ankle dorsiflexion and plantar flexion)

questions.explanation: Calf muscle pump activity increases venous return; combined with early mobilisation and stockings.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When a patient develops a clinically suspected deep vein thrombosis the physiotherapist should:

options.A: Stop exercise of the limb, rest, and refer for urgent medical assessment
options.D: Apply heat and give vigorous exercise

questions.explanation: Exercise or massage may dislodge a thrombus, causing pulmonary embolism.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Buerger-Allen exercises are used in:
questions.explanation: The leg is elevated (vasoconstriction/drain), dependent (vasodilatation), then horizontal, in cycles.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Intermittent claudication is calf pain that:

options.C: Occurs on walking a fixed distance and is relieved by rest

questions.explanation: Caused by atherosclerotic arterial insufficiency; supervised walking programmes improve walking distance.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Venous leg ulcers are typically located:

options.A: On the lateral border of the foot
options.B: Over the medial malleolus (gaiter area) and are treated with graduated compression
options.D: On the toes with a punched-out margin

questions.explanation: Chronic venous hypertension causes lipodermatosclerosis and ulceration; compression bandaging is the mainstay after excluding arterial disease (ABPI).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Complex decongestive therapy for lymphoedema includes:

options.D: Manual lymphatic drainage, compression bandaging, exercise and skin care

questions.explanation: CDT has an intensive phase and a maintenance phase; avoid heat and trauma to the limb.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: After radical mastectomy, which is NOT a part of typical physiotherapy intervention?

options.B: Elevation and positioning of the arm

questions.explanation: Pain medication is prescribed by physicians; physiotherapy prevents lymphoedema and shoulder stiffness.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pre-operative physiotherapy for abdominal surgery includes teaching:

options.B: Deep breathing, effective coughing with wound support and leg exercises

questions.explanation: Education before surgery reduces post-operative pulmonary complications and DVT.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which factor is MOST associated with post-operative pulmonary complications?

options.C: Upper abdominal surgery in a smoker with COPD

questions.explanation: Upper abdominal and thoracic surgery reduce diaphragm function and cough; smoking and COPD increase risk.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A stage 1 pressure ulcer is characterised by:
questions.explanation: Stage 2 partial-thickness loss with a blister; stage 3 full-thickness skin loss; stage 4 exposure of muscle/bone.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which position leaves the heels MOST susceptible to pressure damage?

options.D: Prone with feet over the edge

questions.explanation: In supine the heels bear weight on the mattress; offload with pillows under the calves.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The correct sequence of wound healing phases is:
questions.explanation: Inflammatory (days 0–5), proliferative (days 4–21) and remodelling (21 days to 2 years).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The topical agent commonly used on burn wounds to prevent infection is:
questions.explanation: Silver sulfadiazine has broad antibacterial activity including Pseudomonas; mafenide is an alternative.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Positioning of a burn patient to prevent contractures should be:

options.B: Maintained consistently throughout the day with splinting as needed

questions.explanation: Anti-deformity positioning: axilla abducted, elbow extended, neck extended, hands in the intrinsic-plus position.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Immediately after a split-skin graft the grafted site should be:

options.B: Temporarily immobilised for about 3–5 days to allow graft take

questions.explanation: Shearing disrupts the fragile new vascular connections; movement resumes after the dressing is first checked.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Before exercising, a person with type 1 diabetes should check blood glucose and avoid exercise if:

options.B: Glucose is very low, or high with ketones present

questions.explanation: Hypoglycaemia and ketosis are risks; carry fast-acting carbohydrate and monitor glucose.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A diabetic patient becomes sweaty, shaky and confused during an exercise session. The first action is to:

options.C: Give fast-acting carbohydrate such as glucose

questions.explanation: Treat suspected hypoglycaemia immediately (15 g carbohydrate), then recheck.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Body mass index is calculated as:

options.A: Weight in kg divided by height in metres
options.D: Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared

questions.explanation: WHO classification: overweight 25–29.9, obese ≥30; Asian cut-offs are lower (23 and 25).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Exercise recommended for osteoporosis includes:

options.A: Weight-bearing and resistance exercise with avoidance of forceful spinal flexion

questions.explanation: Weight-bearing exercise maintains bone density; avoid loaded flexion and rotation that increase vertebral fracture risk.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which treatment is inappropriate during an acute flare of rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.explanation: Acute inflammation calls for rest, gentle range of motion and pain relief; stretching/mobilisation aggravates synovitis.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Fibromyalgia is best managed physiotherapeutically with:

options.D: Graded aerobic exercise, education and pacing

questions.explanation: Low-intensity graded aerobic exercise has the best evidence; sleep and stress management are included.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Standard (universal) precautions in physiotherapy include:

options.A: Wearing a mask for every patient
options.C: Avoiding all treatment of HIV-positive patients
options.D: Hand hygiene, gloves for blood/body fluid contact and safe sharps disposal

questions.explanation: Treat all blood and body fluids as potentially infectious; hand washing is the single most important measure.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When treating a patient with dementia the therapist should:

options.D: Use simple short instructions, a consistent routine and demonstration

questions.explanation: Cognitive impairment limits learning of new skills; use demonstration, repetition and familiar tasks.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most effective single intervention to reduce falls in older adults is:

options.D: Multicomponent exercise including balance and strength training

questions.explanation: Tai chi, Otago and balance training reduce fall rate by ~25–40%; also assess home hazards and medication.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pelvic floor muscle training is the first-line treatment for:

options.D: Urge incontinence due to an infection only

questions.explanation: Kegel exercises strengthen the levator ani and urethral sphincter; a 3-month programme is recommended.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In normal pregnancy, exercise should be avoided in the supine position after the first trimester because of:

options.A: Risk of pelvic girdle pain only
options.D: Compression of the inferior vena cava reducing venous return

questions.explanation: The supine hypotensive syndrome causes dizziness and reduced uteroplacental blood flow; use left lateral tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Diastasis recti abdominis is:

options.C: Separation of the two rectus abdominis muscle bellies along the linea alba
options.D: A fracture of the pubic symphysis

questions.explanation: Common in late pregnancy; avoid double leg raises and sit-ups; transversus abdominis activation is taught.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In infants, chest physiotherapy by percussion is performed using:

options.A: Two or three fingers or a small cupped mask, with gentle force
options.C: A mechanical vibrator over the spine
options.D: A cupped adult hand with heavy pressure

questions.explanation: Infants have compliant ribs; gentle techniques with head-down tilt only if medically indicated.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Bronchiolitis in infants is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: RSV causes small airway inflammation with wheeze; treatment is supportive.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Prolonged bed rest produces which cardiovascular effect?

options.D: Orthostatic hypotension and decreased stroke volume

questions.explanation: Deconditioning leads to a loss of plasma volume (~10% in a week) and reduced exercise capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: One MET is approximately equal to an oxygen consumption of:
questions.explanation: 1 MET = resting oxygen consumption (3.5 mL O2 per kg per minute). Light activity 1.6–3 METs, moderate 3–6, vigorous >6.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines (chapter-level reference)
